steps.action: In src/checks.js, remove every strict-mode type error by adding or adjusting JSDoc type annotations only — never change runtime logic, and never change the wording of message strings the tests assert (e.g. 'timeout after Ns', 'exit N: stderr', 'cert valid Nd'). Read src/checks.js with read plus get/recall so whole functions are visible, and read tsconfig.json and package.json to learn the compiler options in play (allowJs/checkJs, strictNullChecks, types: ['node'], declarationDir ./types). Give every function an @param/@returns: type each destructured cfg parameter through an @typedef record with optional members marked, keep possibly-absent detail values optional, and handle caught values ('catch (err)') as unknown — narrow with `typeof err === 'object' && err !== null && 'code' in err` or `err instanceof Error` before reading .code/.message/.name. Never silence a diagnostic with a cast, a `/** @type {X} */ (...)` assertion, @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error or @ts-nocheck — those are rejected by the run. Counters such as `let newest = -Infinity` stay plain numbers; a possibly-null value (e.g. tls getPeerCertificate()) must be guarded by a branch, not asserted. Do not write any file outside src/**. Leave a real edit behind so the tree differs from the step start.

The strict no-emit type check of src/checks.js still reports diagnostics; its raw output is handed to you each attempt. Read src/checks.js (read for the region, get/recall for whole functions) and fix every reported line with JSDoc annotations only — runtime behaviour and every message string stay byte-identical so the existing node --test suite keeps passing (tests assert strings like 'timeout after Ns', 'exit N: stderr', 'cert valid Nd'). Code the checker's complaints rather than defeating them: annotate config params with @typedef/@param records, mark optional members, guard null/undefined branches instead of asserting, and narrow caught `unknown` values with `'code' in err`/`instanceof Error`. If the report names files other than src/checks.js under src/, you may edit those too — bring their diagnostics to the pre-change baseline or better by correcting annotations, never by casts, assertions, @ts-ignore, @ts-expect-error or @ts-nocheck. Iterate until src/checks.js has 0 type errors and nothing else under src/ gained an error, making a real change inside src/** each attempt.
